summary: Writing through a user-defined operator[] is still rejected (error: expression is not assignable), on main (13730886e) and on all 16 stable releases from v1.6.2112 through v1.9.2607; the four older releases predate HLSL 2021 and are not evidence. The repro seeds a known value and writes a different one, so a landed write and a discarded write are distinguishable: neither predicate ever changed, so this has always been a diagnostic and never a silent miscompile. Both explanations in the thread still hold - references are unsupported (Sema::BuildReferenceType), and a trailing const is not part of a member function signature, so a const/non-const operator[] pair is a redeclaration. clang trunk on Compiler Explorer emits the identical diagnostic, with a control pane proving it is not an artefact of incomplete HLSL support.
title: [HLSL 2021] Setter array subscript operator overload
